### Added
- The standalone umbrella's wiring, ported into the connectivity chart and gated on the component toggles the meta chart forwards (roadmap#4348, PRD Q6): with `components.backstage` on, the portal's Agent Platform app-config ConfigMap `agent-platform-backstage-app-config` (the login provider from `global.identity`, one installation `backstage.installationName`, the in-cluster Kubernetes and muster entries, `agentPlatform.fluxServiceAccountName` from the one `kagent.fluxServiceAccountName` value, the skill repositories, the kagent / model-manager API routes when on, the pg block for `backstage.database.engine: postgresql`), the public `HTTPRoute` `backstage.<domain>` and a post-install/post-upgrade config-reload hook that stamps the rendered app-config's checksum into the Backstage Deployment's pod template (`kubectl set env` by label: a no-op while unchanged, a rolling update on a change, nothing on a first install) with its network policy in both flavors (`templates/backstage/`); with `components.mcp-kubernetes` on and muster on, the `MCPServer` CR that registers the server with muster — OAuth, `forwardToken`, `requiredAudiences: [mcp-kubernetes.kubernetesAudience]`, the `infrastructure` tool-group label (`templates/mcp-kubernetes/`); with the new feature switch `components.modelServing` on (an entry without `chart:`: the loop renders no release for it and forwards its flag like every other; a top-level block named after a switch — `modelServing:` — travels with `forwardAllValues` only while the switch is on, so a live connectivity chart that predates the block never sees it), model serving on KServe with vLLM from the `modelServing:` block — the `ClusterServingRuntime`, the seven shipped serving presets and their discovery ConfigMap, the Hugging Face cache PVC, the Kyverno cache policies (`modelServing.policies.enabled: auto`, resolved with the other cluster-shape knobs) and the serving namespace's network policies in both flavors (`templates/model-serving/`, `files/model-serving/`), plus the guard that a model-manager on the `kserve` backend agrees with the layer; the render fails with a clear message when `components.modelServing` is on without `components.kserve-crd` and `components.kserve-resources` (or a cluster that serves the `serving.kserve.io` APIs; `modelServing.kserve.requireApi: false` skips the check); and with `components.kserve-resources` / `components.kserve-llmisvc-resources` on, the controllers' network policies and guards (`templates/kserve/`). The wiring's own keys keep the standalone's names minus `components.` — `backstage.<hostname, parentRefs, installationName, extraScopes, startUrlSearchParams, enabledExtensions, disabledExtensions, skillsRepositories, catalogs, configReload>` and `mcp-kubernetes.kubernetesAudience` live in the chart blocks and are dropped from the values forwarded to the strict component charts (`components.backstage.omitKeys`, `components.mcp-kubernetes.omitKeys`); `modelServing.*` is the standalone's `components.modelServing.*` one-to-one; `components.kserve.*` maps onto the four kserve component toggles (README, "Turning on the standalone's extras"). The seven values blocks of the extras are no longer held back from the connectivity release (`components.agent-platform-connectivity.omitKeys` is empty), the connectivity release `dependsOn` `muster` (the `MCPServer` CRD) and `backstage` `dependsOn` `agent-platform-connectivity` (its pod mounts the ConfigMap rendered there). The kagent UI route guard from the standalone lands too: a `kagent.uiRoute.hostname` override with an oauth2-proxy `redirect-url` still derived from `global.domain` fails the render. `global.identity.ca` (`secretName`, `key`) is declared by the connectivity chart and accepted by the meta chart (`global.identity` is `additionalProperties: true` there — no default, so the `global` block injected into every component release is unchanged). `make verify-wiring` (in CI) asserts off = no object, the objects and guards on, both flavors and the vanilla shape, and the meta chart's forwarding. **No installation needs to act**: every toggle is off on the fleet; the connectivity `HelmRelease`'s values gain the seven blocks and the `modelServing` roster line, its `dependsOn` gains `muster`, and the connectivity chart renders byte-identical objects from them — one Helm revision of that release, no object change, no pod rolled.
